INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.
Application Deadline: Shown in the bottom of the page. All applications must be submitted by 10:00 PM (KST) on the closing date.
Position Grade: G8
Position Scale: International Scale
End date of appointment: 30/06/2028
Salary: Starting range of 76,080 USD
Application Deadline: 04 December 2026, 22:00PM (KST)
INTRODUCTION

GGGI commenced operations in the Pacific in 2014, and it now has programs and projects in 6 member countries including Fiji, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea (PNG), Solomon Islands, Tonga, and Vanuatu, and in two partner countries, Samoa, and Tuvalu. GGGI works in other Pacific Island Countries (PICs) in the Southern and Northern Pacific through its regional programs. The partnership between GGGI and PICs is built on supporting their transition towards low carbon, environmentally sustainable, climate resilient and socially inclusive economies. In addition to national country programs, GGGI proactively implements regional programs and projects in the Pacific that benefit two or more countries for logistical reasons and economy of scale aligned with regional best practice.

Kiribati’s outer island communities face significant barriers in accessing affordable and reliable electricity due to their remoteness and limited infrastructure. To address this challenge GGGI is partnering with the Australian Government funded REnew Pacific Program and Kiribati Green Energy Solutions (KGES) to implement the Kiribati Outer Island Electrification Project (KOIEP). The project will deliver Solar PV Diesel Hybrid Mini Grid systems with Battery Energy Storage on the islets of Ribono in Abaiang and Tabuarorae in Onotoa providing clean reliable and affordable electricity to outer island households. GGGI also supports the wider energy sector in Kiribati working with the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE) and other national partners to advance renewable energy access and reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels.
POSITION SUMMARY

The role will be based at Kiribati Green Energy Solutions (KGES) and will work closely with the KGES CEO and KGES Engineering Manager to provide technical advice, coordinate engineering activities and support the implementation of tasks under the REnew Pacific Kiribati Outer Island Electrification Project (KOIEP). The EE will provide weekly progress updates to the KGES CEO, covering technical activities, implementation progress, key challenges and planned activities. The KGES CEO will remain responsible for overall coordination with the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE), including ensuring that relevant MISE requirements are met and providing formal project updates to the Ministry following internal technical review and clearance.

The EE will also coordinate with the GGGI National Coordinator Officer (NCO) based at MISE to ensure that relevant project information is consolidated and communicated appropriately to the Energy Planning Department (EPD). Where required, the EE may participate in technical discussions with MISE in coordination with the KGES CEO and the NCO. The EE's responsibilities will focus on providing technical advice, engineering coordination, design review, implementation support, and quality assurance in close collaboration with the KGES Engineering Manager and technical team. All activities will be undertaken in accordance with the approved project scope and applicable GGGI, donor, and MISE requirements.
PURPOSE

The Energy Engineer will play a central technical role in the implementation of the REnew Pacific Kiribati Outer Island Electrification Project (KOIEP) and any work that will be assigned by the Country Representative and Regional Energy Lead and agreed in the annual work plan endorsed by MISE. Working closely with KGES, the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy and the Regional Energy Lead, the role will be responsible for performing the following tasks and duties:

Work closely with KGES and MISE on the technical design and implementation of Solar PV Diesel Hybrid Mini Grid systems with Battery Energy Storage for outer island communities in Kiribati ensuring technical quality safety and sustainability.

Collaborate with KGES and the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy to conduct technical assessments, prepare engineering documentation and support procurement and construction activities.

Oversee project delivery for the Kiribati Outer Island Electrification Project including monitoring system performance, managing risks and ensuring compliance with environmental, social and gender inclusive safeguards.
Oversee construction, commissioning and quality assurance of the Solar Mini Grid systems at Ribono and Tabuarorae for the Kiribati Outer Island Electrification Project.
Coordinate closely with the REnew Pacific team to ensure that all project deliverables, milestones and reporting requirements are met on time and to the required quality.
Build local capacity by organizing training programs and providing technical guidance to KGES/EPD engineers, MISE (OIAITs), Island Technicians, Solar Committees and community stakeholders.
Support the KGES Project Management Unit and contribute to reporting, budgeting and stakeholder coordination in line with GGGI and REnew Pacific operational standards.
Conduct technical assessments and feasibility studies for new and ongoing energy projects in Kiribati, as agreed with EPD and included in the endorsed work plan.

Review and recommend approval of detailed system designs, engineering drawings and technical studies prepared by consultants and contractors, maintaining GGGI’s independent technical quality assurance of all works delivered by partners and contractors.
Prepare engineering and technical specifications and tender documentation for renewable energy systems.
Conduct site inspections, quality assurance and acceptance testing to ensure installations meet safety, durability and performance requirements.
ENGAGEMENT
Serve as the primary technical focal point for KOIEP, working closely with the KGES Chief Executive Officer on system design, procurement and implementation matters.

Provide regular updates to the GGGI Country Representative for Kiribati and CEO KGES on project progress and activities on the ground, while reporting technically to the GGGI Regional Energy Lead. The EE will also provide a monthly technical update to the KGES and NCO, who will combine it with the GGGI related energy projects update into a single GGGI energy update to EPD, and will copy EPD on technical, six-monthly and milestone reports at the time they are submitted.

Work within the Energy Coordination protocol agreed between GGGI and MISE. The annual work plan will be prepared in consultation with the NCO, KGES and EPD, and endorsed by MISE before implementation and meetings, consultations and official travel in Kiribati relating to energy will be coordinated through MISE.

Work with the NCO so that EPD receives one consolidated GGGI workplan and progress update and coordinate outer island visits and community consultations with the NCO and MISE to avoid duplicate consultations.

Support embedded project staff and focal ministry officers, ensuring renewable energy system designs comply with national codes, energy act and regulations, international standards and community needs.

Facilitate technical consultations and capacity building with Island Councils, Solar Committees, KGES staff and community representatives at Ribono and Tabuarorae to validate designs and strengthen local technical capacity.
Maintain strong technical partnerships with REnew Pacific and other technical partners to promote innovation, sustainability and knowledge sharing in Kiribati.
DELIVERY

Support the technical implementation of the Solar PV Diesel Hybrid Mini Grid systems at Ribono and Tabuarorae, including engineering design, procurement of equipment and supervision of installation and commissioning.
Support KGES and the Project Management Unit in delivering energy infrastructure aligned with national energy policies/regulations and Act and REnew Pacific program objectives.

Provide technical input to tariff structuring, operations and maintenance planning and investment mechanisms, which are led by MISE and KGES, ensuring alignment with sustainability and resilience goals.

Ensure quality assurance and compliance with engineering standards, environmental safeguards and gender and social inclusion requirements throughout project implementation. Any non-compliance or material risk will be reported to EPD in a timely manner.
Monitor technical progress, identify risks related to design, procurement or implementation, and propose timely engineering solutions to maintain project timelines and quality.

Prepare and contribute to technical sections of project reports, including the six-monthly progress reports and milestone reports required under the REnew Pacific Grant Agreement for KOIEP where applicable. Reports will be shared with MISE at the same time as they are submitted.
Organize and lead technical workshops and training for KGES staff/MISE EPD staff, Solar Committees and MISE OIAITs, KGES Island Technicians on system operation, maintenance and monitoring.

Support procurement planning and execution for technical equipment and services, ensuring specifications meet project requirements and delivery schedules. Support the preparation of supplier and equipment submissions to REnew Pacific for no-objection prior to procurement, in line with Special Condition 3 of the Grant Agreement. Supplier and equipment submissions will be copied to EPD at the same time they are submitted.
Enable technical knowledge transfer to KGES engineers, local technicians and community stakeholders to strengthen long term ownership, operation and maintenance of the systems.
Prepare, before the end of the contract, a handover plan covering documentation, data and equipment and hand over to KGES and EPD.
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Masters in electrical engineering, renewable or sustainable energy, mechanical engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.

At least five (5) years of professional experience in the design, implementation and management of renewable energy infrastructure projects, particularly in developing countries and the Pacific Island region.
Minimum of five years of experience in energy policy or investment project work in energy, climate change, green growth, renewable energy or a related sub sector.

Demonstrated expertise in renewable energy systems, including solar PV, mini grids, battery energy storage and hybrid energy solutions, with hands on experience managing projects in Kiribati or the Pacific region.
Strong technical knowledge of renewable energy technologies, energy transition strategies and climate resilience in Small Island Developing States.

Familiarity with energy policy development, regulatory frameworks and institutional capacity building in the energy sector, including engagement with the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy.

Proven experience delivering infrastructure projects in remote and culturally diverse environments, with an understanding of logistical challenges such as transport, supply chain constraints and access to outer islands.
Experience working with donor funded programs such as the Australian Government's REnew Pacific Program and familiarity with donor contractual, financial and reporting requirements.
Strong skills in stakeholder coordination, working effectively with government agencies, utility providers and community organizations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to produce high-quality technical documentation and deliver presentations to diverse audiences.
Willingness to be based in Kiribati and to travel to outer islands to support project implementation, training and stakeholder engagement.
FUNCTIONAL

Strong understanding of sustainable development and climate resilience in the Kiribati and Pacific Island context, with practical experience in renewable energy policy, infrastructure planning and capacity development.

Demonstrated ability to build relationships and facilitate inclusive consultations with Island Councils, Solar Committees, community groups and government ministries, ensuring culturally respectful engagement and local ownership.
Resourceful and adaptable in developing context specific strategies that respond to the logistical, environmental and social realities of outer island communities in Kiribati.
Proven skills in technical project management, including work planning, budgeting, monitoring, evaluation and risk management.
Experience in energy project financing, including tariff structuring and community based operating models such as Build Own and Operate arrangements.
Knowledge of and commitment to environmental and social safeguards, ensuring designs and implementation are inclusive, gender sensitive and environmentally sound.
Proven leadership in managing technical teams, with a deep appreciation for Kiribati and Pacific values, customs and community dynamics.
High degree of cultural sensitivity and respect for diversity, with a commitment to empowering local communities through inclusive energy solutions.
CORPORATE
Understand and actively support GGGI's mission, vision, and values.
Promote the optimum use of public resources.
Promote an organizational culture of trust, transparency, respect, and partnership.
Process and share information easily.
Manage emotions and stress positively, build rapport, and resolve conflict constructively.
Promote creativity and innovation among staff.
WORK CONDITIONS

The Energy Engineer is a G8 International grade level in GGGI's salary scale. For G8 International grade, the base salary starts from USD 76,080. Determination of base salary is subject to candidate's experience, academic background and internal equity. GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision. In addition, GGGI provides expatriate benefits such as expatriate allowance - equivalent to 20% of the base salary, educational allowance, and other benefits.

Depending on individual circumstances and prevailing job market conditions, the position may be designated as either an international or national position with the terms and conditions of appointment that commensurate with position designation.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
